intro.title: Build JWT auth middleware
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a JWT (JSON Web Token) authentication middleware for a Node.js application. You'll learn how to create a function that intercepts incoming HTTP requests, verifies the JWT from the request headers, and allows or denies access to protected routes. The core programming concept is middleware, which processes requests before they reach your route handlers. You'll use technologies like the jsonwebtoken library and Express.js middleware structure. By the end, you'll have a reusable middleware that secures your API endpoints with token-based authentication.
intro.usecase: JWT auth middleware is a core security pattern in modern web applications, ensuring only authenticated users can access protected resources. You'll implement this in Node.js to secure API endpoints, such as user dashboards, admin panels, or payment forms in e-commerce and SaaS products. For example, when a user logs into a banking app, this middleware validates their token before allowing access to account details or transaction history. As a developer, you'll use this to protect sensitive routes, manage user sessions, and maintain secure, stateless authentication across your services.
